newsitem.title: UK: S&P rates Ras Laffan Liquefied Natural Gas bonds.
newsitem.headline: S&P rates Ras Laffan Liquefied Natural Gas bonds.

text.p: Standard & Poor's said on Tuesday it assigned its BBB plus rating on Ras Laffan Liquefied Natural Gas Co Ltd's offering of $150 million bonds due 2006 and $250 million bonds due 2013.
"The bonds are the first rated debt used in a project financing in the Persian Gulf region," S&P said in a statement.
S&P said the outlook was stable.
It said the ratings on the bonds, which are part of Ras Laffan's financing of its $2.4 billion project in Qatar, incorporated the following risks

-- Several, but not joint, unconditional sponsor completion guarantees (which repay debt if the project does not satisfy certain completion tests --a project strength) that effectively have Mobil Corp's AA rating for 30 percent of the guarantee, but only the State of Qatar's BBB rating for the remaining 70 percent.
-- Even risk related to regional conflicts or disturbances that could temporarily impair liquefied natural gas (LNG) deliverability, and
-- If called upon, the Qatari legal system might not be able to enforce the remedies that the legal and financing documents provide.
However, S&P said the following strengths offset the risks at the BBB plus level.

-- An offshore New York trustee to which all revenues from Korea Gas Corp (Kogas) and others, which are in U.S. dollars are paid and from which all expense, debt service, and equity distributions are paid.
-- The project's strategic importance to Mobil Corp, Qatar, and Kogas, particularly given the multibillion dollar capital commitments to LNG that the buyer and sellers separately have made.
-- Use of commercially proven, current LNG and offshore natural gas productions technology.

-- A take-or-pay Sale and Purchase Agreement (SPA) with Kogas that features the higher of a crude oil based, LNG proxy market price or a minimum floor price that sufficiently guarantees debt service obligations.

-- Five years of natural gas production history from Qatar's North Field, on of the world's largest gas fields, that more than adequately confirm the 7.11 trillion cubic feet of reserves needed to supply the project's Kogas SPA.
-- Construction activities that are on schedule with EPC contracts awarded and signed.
-- An international construction team of the leading LNG process and offshore oil and gas contractors, including JGC/MW Kellogg, McDermott- EPTM/Chiyoda, and Saipem;
-- Mobil's 20 years of LNG experience in Indonesia and more recently, its 10 percent interest in Qatargas, which give Mobil about 12 percent of the world's LNG market share, and

-- A minimum projected debt service coverage ratio of 1.52 and an indenture loan life coverage of 2.22 for a one train project (an LNG production facility) case and an indenture loan life coverage of 2.38 for the two train option.

S&P said Ras Laffan would use the proceeds of the 144a bond offering and a number of export credit agency facilities and commercial bank loans to construct a $2.4 billion, 2.6 million ton per year, single LNG train in Qatar.

"Project and financing documents provide Ras Laffan with the option of building a second train for an additional $1.0 billion if certain tests are met and approved by lenders," the rating agency said.

S&P said project sponsors were Mobil QM Gas Inc, a wholly owned subsidiary of Mobil Corp (AA corporate credit rating, stable outlook) at 30 percent and Qatar General Petroleum Corp. (QGPC) (BBB corporate credit rating, stable outlook) at 70 percent. Korea Gas, which is 50.1 percent owned by the Republic of Korea (AA minus foreign currency rating and stable outlook; AA plus local currency rating) and 34.5 percent owned by Korea Electric Power Co (AA minus foreign currency rating and stable outlook, AA local currecy rating) has entered into a 25-year SPA with Ras Laffan that requires LNG deliveries to begin on or about August 1, 1999.

"The Ras Laffan project benefits from robust economic fundamentals, a highly experienced and committed sponsor (Mobil Corp), and a continuously improving LNG market, which should not change adversely during the next 20 years," the agency said.

"The triple B plus rating, which is a notch higher than the State of Qatar's and QGPC's triple B foreign currency ratings, balances modest credit enhancements contained in the project structure, including Mobil and Qatar guarantees and an offshore trust, with regional event risks closely intertwined with the Qatar and QGPC credit risks."

"These enhancements, combined with the project's strategic importance to its sponsors and Kogas, as LNG buyer, allow Standard & Poor's to conclude that the project's bond rating will not erode. However, debt service coverage ratios with modest upside potential and long-term political risk in the region, as captured by the Qatari foreign currency rating, likely will limit upward rating movement in the next one to three years," S&P said.
